subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.

spec.name: Arasaka-style Riot Interceptor RC-9
spec.description: A heavy corporate riot-control interceptor truck in Cyberpunk 2077 style, with a roof-mounted water cannon turret, neon light bars, armoured plating and corporate livery.
spec.layout: Low, wide, angular armoured assault truck facing +Z. Front: wedge push-bumper with a plough blade, a neon cyan light bar across the grille and magenta underglow. Middle: a chunky armoured cab with a slit windshield, dark tinted glass, side hazard lights and a roof light bar. Rear: a raised armoured cargo bay with a roof turret ring carrying a thick water cannon on a pivoting barrel, a coolant tank and a hose. Six chunky wheels, three per side, sit in armoured wheel arches. The hull is matte graphite with hazard-yellow trim, corporate red-white livery decals, angular panel seams and bright neon (cyan, magenta, amber) strips. All the neon pieces glow. Everything is blocky faceted primitives; detail comes from textures, paints, decals and small fittings.

parts.builds: Lower armoured hull and undercarriage: a long graphite slab frame from z=-3.1 to z=3.0 with sloped sides, a skid plate, side skirts with hazard-yellow chevron paint, three wheel arches per side (cut-out look via dark arch boxes and trim rims), axle housings, a magenta neon underglow strip along each side bottom (glow), rear bumper with a tow hook and red tail lights (glow), exhaust stacks, corporate livery stripe along each flank (red and white SVG decal with a small logo and text 'RC-9 PACIFIER'). Panelled paint on the hull.
parts.attaches: Top face at chassisTop carries the cab and cargo; wheels sit at the axle mounts; the bumper part starts at z=3.0.

parts.builds: Front: wedge plough bumper with a yellow-black hazard-striped blade, a grille with cyan neon bar (glow) and two amber headlights (glow), brush guards and a winch. Armoured cab from z=-0.4 to z=2.7 on the cabFloor: sloped hood, slit windshield with dark glass and a cyan HUD-like reflection texture, side windows with mesh bars, door seams and handles, wing mirrors with small cameras, roof light bar of magenta and cyan segments plus red-blue strobe beacons (glow), antenna array, sensor pod, corporate eye-logo decal on the hood and door numbers. Panelled and weathered paint with grime near the bottom.
parts.attaches: Sits on the chassis at chassisTop and cabFloor; the rear wall meets the cargo bay at z=-0.4; the roof bar is at roofBar.

parts.builds: Rear armoured cargo and utility bay from z=-3.2 to z=-0.4 above chassisTop: a boxy riveted shell with sloped upper edges, a ribbed roof with a flat turret deck at cargoRoof, a round turret ring base with yellow trim, side access hatches with warning stripes and neon amber edge strips (glow), vents with grilles, a rear double door with a warning label texture, a blue pressurised water tank (cylinders on the roof rear with bands, gauge decal and valves), pipes running to the turret, ladder rungs, floodlights on the rear corners and vertical neon cyan accent bars (glow). Hull panelled paint, yellow hazard trim and corporate branding text 'CROWD CONTROL'.
parts.attaches: Sits on chassisTop behind the cab; the turret ring at turretRing on its roof; the tank is behind the ring on the roof.

parts.builds: The roof water cannon on turretRing: a rotating armoured base drum (joint turret) with a yellow ring band and slewing gears, a cradle with side arms, a gunner shield with a slit window and cyan neon edge (glow), the thick cannon barrel (joint cannon) pointing forward along +Z from cannonPivot with a flared nozzle, bands, a pressure gauge (use gaugeTexture), a muzzle ring glowing cyan (glow), supply hoses curving back to the tank, a targeting camera and a magenta laser sight (glow), plus a warning label 'HIGH PRESSURE'. Rigid parts on the turret and cannon joints.
parts.attaches: Turret base on turretRing; barrel pivots at cannonPivot; hoses end at the tank on the cargo roof.

parts.builds: Six chunky armoured wheels on the axle mounts (frontAxle, midAxle, rearAxle at x=±1.2), each on its own wheel joint with the axle along x: a wide faceted rubber tyre (lathe or cylinder with 14 sides) with a tread paint, an outer steel rim with lug nuts (merge per wheel), a hub cap with a small corporate emblem texture and a neon magenta rim ring (glow). Wheel radius 0.55, width 0.5, resting on y=0. Include inner axle stubs and brake discs connecting to the chassis.
parts.attaches: Each wheel is centred on its axle mount and joint, inside the chassis wheel arches.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning out a buildChassis function, defining the bounding box dimensions for the shape and working out how to type the context parameter.

Now I'm placing the wheels at specific x, z, and radius values, then designing dark recessed arch boxes along the hull's outer face around each wheel. I'm sketching the front-view cross-section profile for the main hull — widening from a narrow bottom to a broader top — and planning to extrude that shape along the z-axis with a panelled metal finish.

I'm adding a dark underside skid plate, then working out side skirt segments that sit between the wheel arches, with the gaps calculated so I can apply yellow/black hazard chevron decals to those skirt strips.

Placing a decal for the opposite side facing the other direction, keeping orientation consistent so the chevrons don't look upside down. I'm also planning a livery stripe above the wheel arches, keeping it thin so it clears the arch height, maybe adding a red/white band with text.

Front-at-left reading confirmed for both sides. Now I'm designing the stripe bar graphic with a red background, white accent line, "RC-9 PACIFIER" text, and a small logo circle, sizing the plane and viewBox to match the hull proportions and checking hull height at that band for fit.

Working out the hull's tapering profile so the decal and arch boxes align correctly against the sloped sides, pinning down exact x-coordinates at each y-level to keep edges flush.

I'm also planning the arch trim with thin yellow boxes forming a rim around the top and sides, then designing the axle housings as cylinders tucked beneath the hull with a differential bulb, checking they stay mostly hidden inside the body.

Now I'm adding magenta underglow strips along the hull's bottom edges, positioning them near the wheels so they peek through without clipping through the wheel geometry too obviously.

Now I'm positioning the rear bumper and tail lights on the hull's rear face, with warning-red glow boxes above the bumper and a center strip, plus planning a tow hook and considering exhaust stacks near the rear corners beneath the cargo box.

Finalizing the exhaust stacks with dark caps, then deciding to keep the front end simple with tow eye loops on the flat front face instead of adding slopes or extra plating. For the top deck, I'll skip extra trim lines and focus on basic side vent greebles for visual detail.

Now I'm working out the gap segments between the wheel arches to place yellow skirt chevron panels, calculating the arch boundaries and the small clearance zones between them where the chevron plates will fit.

Writing chevron texture SVG...

Still shaping the hull outline...

I'll switch to a simple angled box for the front plate instead, skipping the frustum complexity. I'm also planning small details like merged bolt spheres along the skirts, cylindrical axle housings with sphere differentials, and a driveshaft cylinder running along the center.

For the wheel arches I want visible axle stubs and suspension arm boxes with a dark leaf spring, keeping the actual axle hidden inside the hull where it wouldn't show anyway. Now I'm thinking about applying glow effects from the kit and picking out the color palette.

Still shaping the arch outline...

Simplifying the hull profile to go vertical then chamfer to a point, with the livery band centered lower to avoid overlapping the arch trims—so I'm lowering the arch tops and trim tops to keep clear separation between all the decorative layers.

I'm adding skirt panels along the lower body and a textured livery decal centered on the side, plus building box and mirror helper functions so panels and decals automatically mirror across both sides. For the decal orientation, I'm working out the correct right/up vectors so the texture faces outward correctly when viewed from outside the vehicle.

Now I'm designing the side livery texture itself: a red base with hazard stripes, a bold "RC-9 PACIFIER" wordmark, a circular logo with a red eye motif near the front, and a slanted white accent block toward the rear, along with glowing tail lights for the back of the vehicle.

Next I'm working out the rear details -- a tow hook assembly, a rear bumper box with a hazard-striped texture plane facing backward, and a sloped front skid plate created by rotating a box slightly along the x-axis to angle it upward.

Adding bolt details...

I'll add small amber side marker light glows near the front and rear of the hull, positioned to avoid overlapping the livery stripe, then move on to actually writing out the full part definitions.
